This page is the general how-to-start illustration: open the box, sort the pieces, start building. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Step 1: white Plate 4 x 12 (b1) is the base canvas.
Step 2: yellow Tile 1 x 2 (b2) and yellow Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b3) sit side by side near the back-left corner of b1. Each rests on b1 only; they sit next to each other, not stacked.
Exact stud ports are not named because the page does not show them precisely enough.
Step 3: one yellow Tile 1 x 2 (b4) and two yellow Tile 2 x 3 (b5, b6) fill the two back rows of the white base b1 next to the wedge b3, forming a yellow row.
Step 4: black Plate 1 x 8 (b7) goes on the third row of b1, in front of the yellow tiles, and a yellow Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b8) goes at the right end of b1.

All five pieces are listed as resting on the base b1 only. The tiles and wedge are placed beside each other, and b7 sits on the base row in front of the tiles. The exact stud positions are not shown clearly enough to name ports.
Step 5: two light bluish gray Plate 2 x 12 (b9 left, b10 right) are added at the two ends of the white base b1. They run away from it at a right angle and form a U shape.

Each is listed as resting only on the white base b1, because only the near end of each plate overlaps the base. The page is too small to tell whether the gray plates also touch the black plate b7 or the yellow wedge b8, so those joins are left out.
Step 6: three white Plate 4 x 12 (b11, b12, b13) are laid edge to edge in front of the base b1, under the two gray Plate 2 x 12 (b9, b10). With b1 they make the 12 x 16 canvas, 16 studs deep.

The two gray plates run along the left and right edges and sit on top of the new white plates. I took each gray plate to rest on all three new plates, and it is already joined to b1 from step 5. Their front ends stop about two studs short of the front edge.
The white plates only touch each other along their long edges, so those links are `contact`. The gray plates hold them together.
Step 7: three blue Tile 2 x 4 (b14, b15, b16) are laid end to end in one 2-wide column down the middle of the canvas, between the two gray plates. The column is 12 studs long.
The column starts on the fourth row, just in front of the black plate b7, and runs toward the front. Their front end goes past the front ends of the gray plates.

Because a 4-stud tile is the same length as a 4 x 12 plate is deep, I took each tile to straddle two white plates: b14 on b1 and b11, b15 on b11 and b12, b16 on b12 and b13. This follows from the row counts, not from a clear view of the page.
Step 8: six yellow Tile 1 x 4 go in the 1-stud white strips outside the gray plates, three on each side. Together they make a yellow border strip 12 studs long on each side.

Left strip (b17, b18, b19): starts level with the black plate row and ends near the front end of the gray plate. Right strip (b20, b21, b22): starts just in front of the yellow wedge b8 and runs to the front edge of the canvas.
The row alignment is estimated from the picture. Left tiles: b17 on b1 and b11, b18 on b11 and b12, b19 on b12 and b13. Right tiles: b20 on b11, b21 on b12, b22 on b13.
The tiles sit beside the gray plates and do not touch them.
Step 9: two yellow Plate 1 x 6 (b23, b24) sit end to end along the front edge of the canvas, one stud deep, to form a yellow border across the full 12-stud width.
Both plates rest on the front white plate b13 only. They are placed in the front row, in front of the gray and blue pieces, so they do not clutch those.
The plates lie in the front rows beside the yellow side tiles. I did not list joins to those tiles, since the page does not show whether they overlap.

Step 10: a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left (b25) and a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b26) are added along the back of the canvas, over the black Plate 1 x 8 (b7). Together they make the black upper edge of the cowl.

Each wedge rests on b7 and on the gray plate at its own end (b25 on b9, b26 on b10). The exact overlap is estimated from the picture. They may also touch the white base b1 or the first blue tile b14, but I did not list those.
Step 11: two black pieces form the bat ears. The left ear (b27) is a Wedge Plate 2 x 4 pointing up at the back-left. The right ear (b28) is a long 27° Wedge Plate 2 x 4 pointing out to the right.

The part icons are small, so the exact types are partly guessed. b27 is taken as lego-51739. b28 is taken as lego-65426 (Right), not the Left version lego-65429. The inventory has two of the first and one of each 27° wedge, so the Left 27° wedge may be used on another page.
Joins are estimated. b27 sits on the black left wedge b25. b28 sits on the black right wedge b26 and the yellow wedge b8 at the right end.
Step 12: three black Plate 1 x 8 (b29, b30, b31) are laid on top of the gray side plates, running from the back toward the front. They make the dark cheeks of the cowl.

The picture does not show clearly where the third plate goes. I placed b29 on the left gray plate b9 and b30 and b31 side by side on the right gray plate b10. It could instead be a second plate on the left.
Each plate is listed as resting only on its gray plate. They may also touch the black wedges b25 and b26 near the back, but this is not clear enough to list.

Step 13: three black Plate 4 x 8 (b32 back, b33 middle, b34 front) are laid across the middle of the canvas. Each is 8 studs wide and 4 deep. Together they cover the blue tiles, the white strips and most of the gray plates, making the black cowl face.

Each plate is listed as resting on everything under it. b32 covers b14, the base b1, b11, the gray plates b9 and b10, and the black 1 x 8 plates b29, b30, b31. b33 covers b15, b11, b12, b9, b10 and the same three black plates. b34 covers b16, b12, b13, b9 and b10. The 8-stud-long black plates only reach the back two rows of 4 x 8 plates.
Exact stud overlap is estimated from the row counts. A strip of gray plate is still visible at the left and right edges beside the front plates.
Step 14: four black wedge plates are added along the lower edge of the black face plates. They fill in the sides and the pointed chin. The tray shows 2x, 1x and 1x of three different pieces.

The part icons are small and I could not tell them apart for certain. I guessed 2x lego-43723 (b35, b36), 1x lego-65429 (b37) and 1x lego-43722 (b38). This matches the inventory: with b25 these use all three black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left, the one black 27° Left wedge, and the second of three black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right.
Their positions are estimated. They are placed at the front corners on the front black plate b34, and also on the gray side plates b9 and b10 where they reach them. Please check against later pages.
Step 15: a black Plate Special 2 x 2 with Only 2 studs (b39) and a tan Plate 1 x 4 (b40) are added at the top of the black face, near the back edge. The tan plate is a skin-colored forehead detail.
The black piece is almost hidden in the result picture, so its place is guessed. I put b39 on the back black plate b32 and b40 partly over b39 and partly on b32. Check against later pages.

Step 16: a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left (b41) and a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b42) are added at the top of the face, one on each side of the tan plate b40. Together they curve the top edge of the cowl between the ears.
Both are listed as resting on the back black plate b32. They may also touch the ear wedges b25 and b26 or the yellow edge, but the page does not make this clear.

Inventory check: the set has only three black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left. I used b25, b35 and b36 earlier, so b41 would be a fourth. This means my guess for the 2x piece in step 14 (b35, b36) was probably wrong, and those two should probably be a different part, such as Wedge Plate 2 x 2 Left lego-24299 or Right lego-24307. Please check this against the step 14 icons.

Step 17: a blue Plate 2 x 6 (b43) goes in the middle of the face. Two tan Plate 1 x 4 (b44, b45) go on either side of it. With the tan plate b40 from step 15 they form a tan frame around the blue plate, open at the front.
All three new pieces are listed as resting on the back and middle black face plates b32 and b33. The overlap is estimated from the row counts. Only part of each tan plate may touch b33.
The tan plates sit next to the blue plate and are not joined to it. They may also touch b40 and b39 at the top, but this is not clear enough to list.
Step 18: two black Plate 2 x 2 Corner (b46, b47) are added, one on each side, at the front end of the tan strips just beside the blue plate. They close in the lower corners of the tan frame.

The box shows 2x of the same piece, and two arrows point to the left and right positions. Both are listed as resting on the middle black plate b33. They may also touch the tan plates b44 and b45 or the black plate b32, but this is not clear enough to list.

Step 19: two tan Plate 2 x 3 (b48 left, b49 right) and two white Plate Special 2 x 2 with Only 2 studs (b50, b51) are added at the front end of the tan frame. The tan plates form the cheeks and the two white pieces sit between them, in front of the blue plate. This is the mouth and chin area.

Joins are estimated from the picture. Each tan plate rests on the black corner plate beneath it (b46 left, b49 on b47 right) and on the middle black face plate b33. Each white piece rests on b33 and on the neighbouring corner plate. The page does not show clearly whether they also touch the tan side plates b44 and b45 or the blue plate b43.
Step 20: one tan Plate 2 x 3 (b52) and two tan Wedge Plate 3 x 3 Cut Corner (b53 left, b54 right) are added in front of the white pieces. They form the tan chin and jaw with an angled outline.

The part icons are small. I took the 1x piece as lego-3021 (Plate 2 x 3, six studs) and the 2x piece as lego-2450 (Wedge Plate 3 x 3 Cut Corner). The tan inventory also has 2x lego-26601 (2 x 2 Cut Corner) and 1x lego-3022, which could be what is shown. Please check against later pages.
Joins are estimated. b52 rests on the front black plate b34 and the middle plate b33. b53 and b54 rest on the tan plates b48 and b49 from step 19 and on b34.

Step 21: a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left (b55), a black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b56) and two black Tile Round 1 x 1 Quarter (b57, b58) are added at the front corners of the face. They shape the pointed lower edge of the cowl around the chin.

The wedges are listed as resting on the front black plate b34. The two quarter tiles are tiny and hard to see in the picture, so I guessed they cap the outer corners of the tan jaw wedges (b57 on b53, b58 on b54). Please check against later pages.
The black Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left count is now 4 in my numbering (b25, b35, b36, b55) and the set has only 3. The step 14 guess (b35, b36) is the likely error, as noted earlier.
Step 22: the model is turned over to show the underside of the four white 4 x 12 plates. A white Plate 1 x 10 (b59) is added along the long outer edge of the back plate b1, on its underside.

It is listed as joined to b1 only, because it sits along that plate's edge. The plate is 10 studs long and sits on the underside, so it is probably used to hold a bracket or hanging element in later steps.

Step 23: on the underside, near the back edge, a light bluish gray Plate 1 x 4 (b60) and two white Plate 1 x 3 (b61, b62) are added. The page shows the gray plate and one white plate already seated. Red arrows show the other white plate dropping in. These form a small mounting block for hanging.
Joins are estimated. The gray plate b60 sits on b1 only. Each white 1 x 3 sits on b1 and on the white 1 x 10 plate b59, which runs along the edge. The picture does not show every stud overlap.

Step 24: on the underside, a white Plate Special 3 x 2 with Rounded End and Hole (b63) goes next to the gray plate b60. Two white Hinge Plate 1 x 2 (b64, b65) are also added. In the picture one hinge is already seated at the right end and the other is being lowered by red arrows. These make the back hanger or stand.

Joins are estimated. b63 sits on the gray plate b60 and the back white plate b1. The hinge b64 sits on b60 and b63. The hinge b65 sits on the white 1 x 3 plate b61. Which hinge goes where cannot be told from the picture, since both are the same part.
The hinge plates each have a hinge finger, but nothing is attached to it on this page, so no hinge join is listed yet.

Step 25: a second white Plate 1 x 10 (b66) is added on the underside along the back edge. It lies over the first 1 x 10 plate b59 and the white 1 x 3 plates b61 and b62. It covers the mounting block and leaves only the hinge area showing.
Joins are estimated from the picture. The plate could also touch the hinge plates b64 and b65 or the gray plate b60, but the page does not show this clearly.

Step 26 is a separate sub-assembly, a U-shaped white handle or stand frame. It is built apart from the canvas. Two white elbow tubes (b68, b69) are linked by the red Technic Axle 2 Notched (b67), which goes into one crosshole of each. A Technic Axle 11 (b70, b71) goes into the other crosshole of each elbow, making two long arms. The arms are marked '11' on the page.
The parts tray also shows 2x hinge cylinder (lego-57360, white), but steps 1 to 3 do not use them. I assume they are used on a following page, so they are not added yet.
Each axle part has a single port, axle.1, so the same port name is used for both ends of the red axle. The two elbows are not touching each other. They are only linked through the red axle.

Step 4 (page 33): a white Hinge Cylinder 1 x 2 (b72, b73) is pushed onto the free end of each Technic Axle 11 (b70, b71). The U-shaped frame from page 32 is then clicked onto the two white hinge plates (b64, b65) on the underside of the canvas. This makes a fold-out stand. The page also gives a 1:1 axle length guide, labeled 11.

Which cylinder goes with which hinge plate is assumed. b72 on b70 goes to b64, nearer the middle ring plate b63, and b73 on b71 goes to b65 at the right. The two hinge plates are the same part, so this is a guess from the picture.
The hinge joins are revolute because the stand is meant to swing.

Step 27: on the underside, two white Brick 1 x 16 (b74 left, b75 right) go down the two long edges of the canvas. A white Brick 1 x 10 (b76) closes the front edge between them. With the two 1 x 10 plates at the back (b59, b66) this makes a white frame around the back of the canvas, covering the stand mount.

Each 1 x 16 brick runs the full 16-stud depth, so it sits on all four white plates (b1, b11, b12, b13). The 1 x 10 brick sits on the front plate b13 and touches the ends of the 1 x 16 bricks. Those touches are listed as `contact`.
The red-arrow stand frame and hinge parts stay inside the frame.

Step 28: four light bluish gray Brick Round 1 x 1 Open Stud (b77 to b80) are pushed onto the four inside corner studs of the frame on the underside. They act as small feet or spacers so the canvas can sit or hang. The red arrow shows one going into the front-left corner.
The two back ones (b77, b78) sit on the back white plate b1, and the two front ones (b79, b80) sit on the front white plate b13. Exact studs are not named because the page does not show them clearly.

Step 29: four white Plate Round 2 x 2 with Rounded Bottom (b81 to b84) are pushed onto the four corners of the frame. They sit over the round 1 x 1 bricks from step 28 and make rounded feet for the finished canvas.

Each one sits on a round brick (b77 to b80) and on the corner studs of the frame bricks beside it. Back-left b81 is on b77, b74 and b66. Back-right b82 is on b78, b75 and b66. Front-left b83 is on b79, b74 and b76. Front-right b84 is on b80, b75 and b76. The corner studs are inferred from the frame layout, not clearly shown.

Step 30: the model is turned face-up again. Three black pieces are added to finish the cowl outline: a Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Left (b85), a Wedge Plate 3 x 2 Right (b86) and a Plate Special 2 x 2 with Only 2 studs (b87).

The icons are small and the picture changes are hard to compare with earlier pages. The piece types are guessed from icon shapes, and the positions are guessed too. I assume all three sit on the front black plate b34. Check against later pages.

The black wedge counts in my numbering exceed the inventory (3 Left and 3 Right). Some earlier black wedge guesses are wrong. The 2 x 2 Cut Corner or the 2 x 2 wedges (lego-24299, lego-24307) are likely what was used in steps 14 and 21.
Step 31: four black Brick Sloped 30 1 x 2 x 2/3 (b88 to b91) are added around the face to shape the cowl.

Their exact positions are not clear from the picture. I guessed two on the upper edges beside the tan strips, resting on the tan plates b44, b45 and the back black plate b32, and two at the lower cheeks on the front black plate b34. Please check against later pages.

Step 32: two black Plate 3 x 3 (b92 left, b93 right) are laid side by side over the upper part of the face. They cover the tan frame and most of the blue plate, leaving only the front end of the blue plate and the white eye pieces showing. This forms the black cowl brow.

Joins are estimated. Both plates are listed as resting on the blue plate b43, the tan plate b40, the back black plate b32, and the tan side plate on their own side (b44 left, b45 right). The slopes from step 31 may sit under or beside them, but the picture does not make this clear, so no joins to them are listed.

Step 33: the white eye slit is added on the black brow. A white Tile 1 x 4 (b94) goes in the middle. A white curved wedge brick goes on each end to make the pointed ends of the eye. They sit on the two black 3 x 3 plates b92 and b93.

The two wedge icons are similar. I assigned the Left one (b95, lego-29120) to the left end and the Right one (b96, lego-29119) to the right end. They could be swapped. The tile is listed as resting on both 3 x 3 plates, since it spans the join between them.
The white Wedged Curved bricks and the white Tile 1 x 4 are the white-colour variants in the inventory.

Step 34: two tan Plate 2 x 3 (b97, b98) and one tan Wedge Plate 4 x 2 Right (b99) are laid over the middle of the face. They cover the blue plate and the white pieces, leaving a narrow white eye slit above and a white slit below. This forms the tan skin of the face.
Joins are estimated. They overlap the blue plate b43, the white 2 x 2 pieces b50 and b51 and the tan side strips b44 and b45. The page does not show which plate sits over which.
The tan Plate 2 x 3 count is now 5 in my numbering (b48, b49, b52, b97, b98), which equals the inventory (5).
Step 35: one tan Plate 1 x 4 (b100) and two shorter tan plates (b101, b102) are added on top of the tan face to build up the nose and cheek relief.

The 1x icon shows four studs, so I took it as lego-3710. The 2x icon shows three studs, so I took it as lego-3623 (Plate 1 x 3, tan). This matches the inventory, since the tan Plate 1 x 4 count (4) would be exceeded otherwise.
Exact positions are estimated from the picture. b100 sits on b97 and b99. b101 sits on b97. b102 sits on b98.
Step 36: one tan Plate 2 x 2 (b103) and two tan Wedge Plate 2 x 2 Cut Corner (b104 left, b105 right) are added to the lower part of the tan face. They round off the chin and mouth edge.

This page changes the picture only a little, so the placement is guessed. b103 is on the chin plate b52 and the two tan 2 x 3 plates. b104 and b105 are on the jaw wedges b53 and b54 and the 2 x 3 plate on their side.
The tan Plate 2 x 2 and tan Cut Corner counts now match the inventory (1 and 2).
Step 37: one black Plate 2 x 4 (b106) is added on the right side of the face, over part of the white eye slit. This shapes the right eye or brow.

Its position is estimated from the picture, which changes very little. It is listed as resting on the right black 3 x 3 plate b93 and on the white eye pieces b94 and b96. The count of black Plate 2 x 4 (1 of 2) is well within the inventory. The second may be used on the next page.
Step 38: two black Wedge Plate 2 x 4 (b107 left, b108 right) are added over the white eye slit, one for each eye. They give the angry slanted brow look.
Joins are estimated. b107 sits on the left 3 x 3 plate b92, the white tile b94 and the left eye wedge b95. b108 sits on the right 3 x 3 plate b93 and the black Plate 2 x 4 b106.

Inventory check: the set has only 2 black Wedge Plate 2 x 4 (lego-51739). These two use both. So b27 in step 11 was probably the Left 27° wedge lego-65429 (the other ear), not a 51739. This should be fixed when the pages are merged.
Step 39: the second black Plate 2 x 4 (b109) goes on the left side of the face, over the left eye. This mirrors b106 on the right in step 37 and completes the pair.
Joins are estimated. It sits on the left black 3 x 3 plate b92 and the left white eye pieces b94 and b95. The page changes little from the one before.

Step 40: two black Brick Curved 2 x 1 No Studs (b110, b111), one black Wedged Curved 2 x 1 Left (b112) and one black Wedged Curved 2 x 1 Right (b113) are added over the eyes. They round off the brows and leave the white eye slits thin.

The icons are small. I put the Left wedged brick on the left eye over b109 and the Right one on the right eye over b106. A curved brick goes on each eye plate. The left/right assignment could be swapped.
Joins are estimated and the pieces could also touch the 3 x 3 plates b92 and b93 or the eye wedges b107 and b108.

Step 41: a black Brick Sloped 45 2 x 2 Double (b114) and a black Brick Sloped 45 2 x 1 Triple (b115) are added at the center of the forehead, between the eyes. The arrow shows the larger slope dropping in. These shape the center peak of the cowl.

The two icons are small. I took the larger slope as lego-3043 and the smaller as lego-15571. I assumed b114 spans both 3 x 3 plates (b92, b93) at the center and b115 sits beside it on b92. Please check against later pages.

Page 49 is a usage illustration. The stand frame (b68, b69, b70, b71, b72, b73) swings out on its hinges (b64, b65) from the back of the canvas so the model stands up. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 50 shows the finished Batman Brick Sketch standing upright on its fold-out stand. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 52 is the back cover: a product-feedback prize advert and legal text. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
